About us
Crypto.com is building the regulated home for prediction markets and derivatives in the United States. Through Crypto.com Derivatives North America and OG.com we operate a CFTC-designated contract market and a registered clearinghouse. OG.com Prediction Markets lists event contracts on sports, politics, economics, culture, and crypto, including single-event contracts and combos.
 
The problem you'll solve
It's Saturday night in the US. A partner broker messages: their customers' orders are stuck, and their support queue is filling up. You do not yet know if it is our gateway, their routing, the market data feed, or the settlement logic. People who can fix it are in the US, in Asia, or asleep. Today, whoever sees the message first owns it. That is the gap.
You are the single owner of every production incident that touches OG.com Prediction Markets, the exchange, the clearinghouse, or our partner brokers, from the first alert to the final review. You do not write the fix. You decide who does, within minutes. You keep every affected partner current. You make the risk call on what happens in the next 20 minutes, the next 3 hours, and on Monday morning. Root cause is identified in the first 30 minutes. An issue does not sit open for four hours.
A platform failure usually hits many partners at once, not one. You run that room.
You report to the SVP of Product. You do not have a team on day one. Within 6 to 12 months, a person who is good at this builds the rotation and owns the partner relationships that come with it.
What you decide: severity, who gets paged, the live timeline, every partner update while the incident is open, and the recommendation to pause, halt, cancel, or keep trading. The on-call approver approves a pause or halt. Exchange Operations owns the listing and the settlement call. Engineering owns the code.




What you'll actually do:
• Own the incident. You are first on the scene for your shift and the escalation point when it matters most, which is the weekend. You classify severity, open the bridge, and pull in Engineering, Exchange Operations, Technical Support, Clearing, and Compliance. One timeline. One owner. If a page goes unanswered, you escalate.

• Run the partner side. You are the named contact for partner brokers and FCMs while the incident is live. You get their engineers on the same bridge, split what is confirmed from what is still unknown, and update them on a fixed cadence. Partners should never learn about our incident from their own customers.

• Make the market call. You judge whether trading is still fair and orderly and recommend pause, halt, cancel, or continue. An exchange that is up while a front end is down, so some participants cannot cancel resting orders, is still an incident. Error-trade, settlement-correction, and emergency-action decisions follow the rulebook and are written down as they happen.

• Keep the regulatory clock. You know which incidents need prompt notice to the CFTC and you get Compliance the facts while the incident is still live. You track the rulebook timers: 30-minute notice on a busted trade, the 24-hour settlement-error window, and the 24-hour filing deadline for emergency rules.

• Investigate the incidents that are not outages. A listing that does not match the real event. A disputed result. A combo with a voided leg. A sports or event feed that is late, missing, or contradicts another source. You assemble the rules, the official outcome, and the evidence so Exchange Operations can call it correctly and on time.

• Close it and hand it over. The record stays current, including who approved each decision. Monday teams pick up open items from your handoff without calling you. You run a blameless review, write the root cause, and track every action, ours and the partner's, until it is closed. Partners get a written report their compliance teams can reuse.

• Get ahead of the peaks. Before the Super Bowl, March Madness, election night, and NFL Sunday, you run readiness reviews and joint drills with partner FCMs. You own the runbooks, the severity matrix, the escalation trees, and the fixes you send back to Engineering.

Requirements:
• You have been the incident commander. You have led major production incidents end to end, as incident commander, incident manager on call, or the person a command center calls when something is on fire, in trading, clearing, brokerage, payments, or another always-on business. You can walk us through one minute by minute: what you saw, who you pulled in, what you decided in the first 30 minutes, and what changed afterwards.

• You have run an incident across company lines. Part of the fix belonged to a partner, vendor, or counterparty you did not control, and you kept both sides moving. Several of them were affected at once.

• You make the call with incomplete information. You can show a time you chose the 20-minute action, the 3-hour action, and the Monday action, and you can say what you would do differently.

• You are technical enough to triage. You can read logs and dashboards, query with basic SQL, and send an API error to the right team the first time. You do not need to write production code.

• You write under pressure. You have a status update, a partner notice, or an incident report that is accurate, calm, and useful to someone who was not in the room.

• You are hands-on. This seat is not a manager who waits for a readout. You run the bridge.

Preferred:
• Exchange, clearinghouse, or FCM experience: production operations, market operations, a control desk, or client technical support at a CFTC- or SEC-regulated venue or broker.

This role sits within SOX Compliance and is the senior technical authority for IT controls in the SOX program. You will set the strategy for ITGCs, IT application controls, and the controls over private key management and digital asset custody. Internal Audit independently tests the controls you own.

You will own the ITGC SOX program, building the control framework, testing approach, and evidence standards from the ground up. This is a hands-on role with real program ownership at a crypto exchange. The technology stack spans blockchain-native infrastructure, digital asset custody systems, and on-chain and off-chain processing, and engineering changes at a pace most companies never see. The systems are complex, the deployments are frequent, and the controls are consequential.

 


THE OPPORTUNITY

 - Strategy & program ownership
   
   - Own the enterprise IT SOX strategy and roadmap, covering ITGC, ITAC, and digital asset and key management controls across all in-scope entities and jurisdictions.
   
   - Define the scoping methodology and risk assessment for IT SOX, including in-scope applications, infrastructure, wallet and custody systems, and third-party and service-organization dependencies.
   
   - Set control design standards and own the control framework. Design controls that fit modern engineering practices (CI/CD, infrastructure as code, cloud) and don’t slow them down.
   
   - Set the standard for management testing and evidence. Direct co-sourced and matrixed resources, and review the quality of their work.
   
   - Use AI-enabled workflows, continuous controls monitoring, and data analytics to move IT SOX from periodic testing toward scalable, automated assurance.
   
   Private key management & digital asset controls
   
   - Own SOX control design and coverage for the full private key lifecycle: generation, storage, access, signing and approval workflows, rotation, backup and recovery, and retirement.
   
   - Assess controls over key custody architectures, such as HSMs, MPC, multi-signature, and hot/warm/cold wallet structures, including segregation of duties, quorum and approval controls, and privileged access.
   
   - Evaluate how key management and custody controls support the existence, completeness, and safeguarding of customer and corporate digital assets and their financial reporting implications.
   
   - Assess controls over on-chain and off-chain transaction processing, reconciliation of wallets to ledgers, and reliance on blockchain data and third-party custodians or service organizations.
   
   - Be the SOX authority on emerging digital asset risks and decide how the control framework should respond as products, chains, and custody models evolve.
   
   Deficiency evaluation & remediation
   
   - Lead evaluation of control deficiencies, including root cause analysis and severity and pervasiveness assessments, and recommend classification (control deficiency, significant deficiency, or material weakness).
   
   - Own remediation strategy for open ITGC and key management findings. Drive executive-level accountability with Engineering, Security, and Infrastructure leaders.
   
   - Escalate gaps and delays directly to senior leadership. Report status to the Audit Committee as required.
   
   - Coordinate with Internal Audit so remediated controls are ready for independent validation.
   
   Executive & external stakeholder engagement
   
   - Be the senior SOX voice to the CFO, CISO, CTO, Controller, and the Audit Committee on IT control posture, risks, and remediation.
   
   - Lead the external auditor relationship on IT matters: audit strategy, reliance and scoping decisions, walkthroughs, and resolution of disagreements.
   
   - Serve as a trusted advisor to engineering and security leaders, translating audit and control requirements into practical engineering decisions.
   
   - Partner with Internal Audit, ERM, the business process SOX lead, and co-sourced providers to align coverage across the full assurance program.
   
   - Mentor SOX and risk team members and raise the technical bar across the function.

 


WHAT YOU BRING

 - 10+ years in SOX compliance, IT audit, internal audit, or external audit, with deep ITGC experience and a record of owning programs at enterprise scale.

 - Direct, hands-on experience with crypto and private key management controls, including designing, assessing, or auditing controls over key custody, wallet infrastructure, signing, and digital asset safeguarding. This is a must-have.

 - Experience in a crypto exchange, custodian, fintech, or payments company with complex, rapidly evolving infrastructure.

 - CISA and CPA certifications required. Candidates with one who are actively pursuing the other will be considered.

 - Expert knowledge of ITGC frameworks, SOX 404, COSO, COBIT, and PCAOB standards, with the judgment to make and defend scoping, reliance, and deficiency-classification decisions.

 - Strong technical fluency in how systems, databases, cloud infrastructure, and deployment pipelines work.

 - Proven ability to connect an ITGC or key management failure to its impact on business process controls and the financial statements.

 - Experience working with external auditors (Big 4 preferred) and presenting to Audit Committees and senior executives.

 - Experience across multi-entity structures or multiple jurisdictions.

 - Exceptional communicator who earns credibility with both engineers and finance executives.




NICE TO HAVES

 - Experience building or scaling an IT SOX program in a growth-stage or first-year SOX company.

 - Familiarity with CI/CD, GitLab or similar version control, and cloud infrastructure (AWS, GCP).

 - Familiarity with SOC 1/SOC 2 reliance for custodians and service providers, and with proof-of-reserves or similar attestations.

 - Familiarity with audit and GRC platforms such as AuditBoard or Workiva.

 - Familiarity with AI-assisted compliance tools and willingness to adopt new technologies.

In eight years time, Bitvavo has established itself as the market leader in the Netherlands and one of the largest in Europe, with over two million users exchanging tens of billions of digital assets a year.

What is the role about

As a fast paced, highly targeted and highly regulated company, security is more important here than most other companies. That means your impact can be much more material, this role is about working with our brothers and sisters in product and engineering and building security through collaboration. It’s about being an engineer who knows how to use automation and tooling to get more done at pace and to scale security’s impact.

The role includes ‘whole of product’ security - Application, architecture and infrastructure. You’ll understand deeply the threats posed to us by threat actors and where to focus our attention, you’ll be the kind of person who enjoys building long lasting relationships, making impact by really moving the needle and scaling through automation so you are always focussed on the highest value work.



How will you make an impact

 - Threat modelling: Taking an attackers lens on what’s being built and understanding how it could be abused/targeted and being able to bring others on the journey through clear communication.

 - Pen testing/Red teaming/Vuln discovery: Being the threat actor but with a whitebox approach, thinking about what tools can you build to help scale these processes. Thinking about how we bring in more data to find the right issues and surface them with appropriate prioritisation.

 - Communication and relationships: Bringing teams on side by working together with the attackers lens, collaboratively designing best of breed security controls that mitigate threads and support the business and our customers by making them as slick as possible.

 - Going deep on existing MO’s and industry attack knowledge: Understanding deeply the attackers, their motivations and evolving techniques, performing evaluations of our controls to ensure they hold up, continuously iterating and educating.



How will you be successful?

 - Backend/frontend development background with a transition into security engineering

 - 5+ years of experience in secure software development and AppSec

 - Demonstrable record of delivering real world security improvements

 - Deep experience of scaling security through automation including AI and slick processes

 - Experience with Kubernetes, containers and CI/CD

 - Strong AWS and/or GCP experience

 - Strong understanding of AuthN/AuthZ, API security, AI Security and OWASP Top 10

 - Experience with tools such as Burp, Wiz, Snyk, Semgrep, Bug bounty and SAST platforms

 - Experience in fintech, payments, crypto or other regulated industries is a big plus

 - Strong analytical and problem-solving skills, with the ability to think like an attacker to anticipate and prevent security issues

Role Purpose

Lead the establishment and ongoing oversight of the Pakistan entity’s independent Compliance function and Anti-Money Laundering, Counter-Terrorist Financing and Counter-Proliferation Financing (AML/CFT/CPF) framework.

During the pre-licensing phase, the role holder will lead Compliance-owned licensing deliverables, develop the local control framework and assess operational readiness. Following licensing, the role holder will discharge the entity’s CO/MLRO responsibilities, advise the Board and senior management, and maintain effective engagement with PVARA, the Financial Monitoring Unit (FMU) and other relevant authorities.

The role combines CO and MLRO responsibilities, subject to applicable regulatory requirements and any required regulatory acceptance or approval. The suitability of the combined arrangement will be reviewed periodically, considering independence, conflicts, capacity, resources and the entity’s nature, scale and complexity.

Key Responsibilities

•

Licensing and Operational Readiness

•

Lead Compliance-owned components of the PVARA licensing application and coordinate relevant inputs from Legal, Business, Risk, Finance, Operations and Technology.

•

Develop and maintain a regulatory obligations register, licensing deliverables tracker and local implementation roadmap.

•

Assess gaps between group policies, systems and controls and applicable Pakistan requirements; oversee localisation and track remediation.

•

Establish local Compliance and AML/CFT/CPF policies, governance arrangements, escalation procedures and regulatory reporting processes.

•

Define local control requirements for customer onboarding, transaction monitoring, sanctions screening, Travel Rule compliance and suspicious transaction reporting.

Assess the suitability and readiness of local, group-provided and outsourced controls, including relevant pre-launch testing.

•

Establish, administer and maintain a documented, risk-based Compliance Management System (CMS) proportionate to the entity’s activities and risk profile.

•

Advise the Board, relevant committees and senior management on applicable legal and regulatory requirements, licence conditions and regulatory developments.

•

Develop and execute a risk-based Compliance Monitoring and Testing Plan; document findings, agree remediation ownership and deadlines with accountable functions, independently validate closure, and escalate overdue or inadequate remediation.

•

Oversee compliance with applicable conduct, customer protection, complaints-handling, client-asset and market-integrity requirements, according to the entity’s licensed activities.

•

Review proposed products, services and material business changes from a local compliance perspective, identifying requirements, restrictions and necessary controls.

•

Ensure material non-compliance is investigated, promptly escalated and remediated, and notified to PVARA where required.

•

Maintain regulatory submission and commitment trackers, overseeing timely and accurate Compliance-owned responses and escalating dependency risks.

•

Act as the primary Compliance liaison with PVARA for supervisory engagement, inspections and information requests.

•

Develop and oversee Compliance training for employees, senior management and relevant key individuals.

•

AML/CFT/CPF and Financial Crime

•

Establish, implement and maintain the entity’s AML/CFT/CPF framework, aligned with applicable Pakistan legislation, regulatory requirements and relevant directions or guidance.

•

Lead the enterprise-wide financial crime risk assessment and oversee risk-based mitigation measures.

•

Oversee customer due diligence, beneficial ownership identification, customer risk assessment, enhanced due diligence and ongoing monitoring.

•

Oversee transaction monitoring, sanctions screening and targeted financial sanctions controls, including escalation and action on relevant alerts.

•

Oversee virtual asset-specific controls, including blockchain analytics, risks associated with unhosted wallets and Travel Rule compliance where applicable.

•

Receive and assess internal suspicious activity referrals, determine whether external reporting is required, and submit suspicious transaction reports to the FMU within applicable deadlines.

•

Exercise independent judgement on suspicious transaction reporting without requiring business approval, while maintaining confidentiality and preventing tipping-off.

•

Manage the entity’s FMU/goAML registration, access arrangements and reporting processes, as applicable.

•

Ensure required customer, transaction and investigation records are retained for applicable periods and remain accessible and retrievable.

Liaise with the FMU and other competent authorities on financial crime matters and oversee relevant information requests.

•

Oversee AML/CFT/CPF training and awareness, tailored to employees’ responsibilities and exposure to risk.

Governance, Reporting and Control Assurance

Provide periodic reports to the Board or designated committee on Compliance and AML/CFT/CPF effectiveness, material risks, incidents, findings and remediation progress.

•

Escalate urgent or material matters promptly rather than waiting for scheduled reporting.

•

Attend relevant Board and committee meetings and provide independent advice and challenge.

•

Assess and oversee group-provided and outsourced Compliance/AML services, including local regulatory suitability, service standards, data access, management information and escalation arrangements.

•

Oversee delegated Compliance and AML/CFT/CPF activities and remain accountable for discharging the CO/MLRO responsibilities, without displacing the responsibilities of the entity, Board, senior management or operational control owners.

•

Coordinate with Risk and Internal Audit, while preserving the distinction between Compliance oversight and independent audit assurance.

•

Support periodic review of the role holder’s continuing fitness, propriety and suitability, including the required review of the MLRO appointment.

•

Maintain effective handover and suitably qualified cover arrangements for absences, consistent with applicable regulatory requirements.

Qualifications and Experience

Essential

A degree in law, finance, business or a related discipline, or an equivalent relevant professional qualification.

•

At least eight years’ relevant Compliance and/or AML/CFT experience in financial services, including at least three years in a senior Compliance, MLRO or equivalent leadership role.

•

Strong knowledge of Pakistan’s financial regulatory and AML/CFT framework, including the Virtual Assets Act, applicable PVARA regulations, the Anti-Money Laundering Act and FMU reporting requirements.

•

Demonstrable understanding of virtual asset business models and their financial crime, conduct and operational risks.

•

Practical experience with customer due diligence, transaction monitoring, sanctions screening, investigations and suspicious transaction reporting.

•

Experience developing risk assessments, policies, monitoring programmes and Board-level reporting.

•

Ability to translate regulatory requirements into workable business, operational and technology controls.

•

Be resident in Pakistan by the date of the formal CO/MLRO appointment and maintain residency as required under applicable regulations.

•

Fluency in English and Urdu.

Desirable

•

Professional certification such as CAMS, an ICA qualification or an equivalent Compliance/AML credential.

•

Experience in virtual assets, exchanges, fintech or digital financial services.

•

Experience supporting a regulatory licence application or establishing a local Compliance function.

•

Experience engaging with PVARA, FMU, SECP, SBP or other relevant Pakistani authorities.

•

Familiarity with blockchain analytics tools and Travel Rule solutions.

•

Experience overseeing centralised group services and outsourced control arrangements.

Key Competencies

•

Independence, integrity and sound judgement.

•

Confidence to challenge senior management constructively.

•

Clear communication with regulators, the Board and cross-functional teams.

•

Strong analytical, investigative and problem-solving skills.

•

Effective prioritisation in a developing regulatory environment.

•

Ability to build a local control framework while working within a global organisation.

Authority and Independence

•

Direct access to the local Board or designated committee, including the ability to escalate without prior management clearance.

•

Timely and unrestricted access to relevant records, systems, personnel and management information necessary to discharge the role, subject to applicable confidentiality and data-handling requirements.

•

Adequate resources and suitably qualified support proportionate to the entity’s activities and risk profile.

•

No client-facing, sales or other responsibilities that compromise independence, create material conflicts or impair CO/MLRO duties.

•

Remuneration arrangements that do not link the role holder’s performance to sales or revenue targets.

•

Group reporting arrangements that do not restrict local regulatory accountability, Board access or independent MLRO decision-making.

•

Board oversight of appointment, replacement and removal, with regulatory approvals or notifications completed as applicable.

A game goes to overtime. A player gets scratched an hour before puck drop. An election result gets called at 2am. You’re the one who makes sure our markets reflect reality: accurately, on time, and within CFTC standards.
This is an operations role at the center of our predictive markets business. You’ll own markets from the initial idea through final settlement. You’ll work with partners to build new products, write the rules that govern them, monitor live events, and make the call when an outcome isn’t clear. When something goes wrong, you’ll figure out what happened, fix it, and make sure it doesn’t happen again. You’ll have real ownership from day one and a direct say in how our operations grow.


Responsibilities:
• Build and oversee markets from idea through settlement, working with partners and internal teams to define the product, the data behind it, and the rules that govern it.

• Support daily exchange operations across production and test environments, including listing, scheduling, end-of-day processing, and settlement.

• Monitor live events and make sure markets open, close, and settle accurately and on time.

• Verify outcomes against authoritative sources. When sources disagree or a result changes, work out the right answer and document why.

• Investigate and resolve incidents under time pressure, understand the impact on customers and partners, and keep a full audit trail to enact automated improvements.

• Analyze trading and position data to support settlements, reviews, and partner requests.

• Partner with finance, legal, and development teams to escalate problems and collaborate on solutions.

• Work with developers to synchronize automation with settlement rules and the structure of the data we ingest.

• Use scripting and AI to automate repetitive work, stress-test rules, and build tools that make the team faster.

• Find gaps in our processes and close them. If something is done manually twice, it should probably be a tool.

• Provide periodic off-hours and weekend coverage as needed to support live market operations.

• Strong analytical skills and comfort working with data in spreadsheets, databases, and operational tools.

• A sports fan with a feel for markets. You follow the storylines, know the leagues, and understand why the details matter.

• An instinct for edge cases. You think through every scenario before it becomes a problem.

• Strong research skills. You find the authoritative source, not just the first result.

• Clear, fast writing for both technical and non-technical audiences.

• A working understanding of APIs, data structures, and how data moves from a source into a system.

• Flexibility to move across disciplines and work effectively with internal teams and outside partners.

• Comfort in a mission-critical environment with live production stakes.

• A bachelor’s degree in Economics, Finance, Mathematics, Computer Science, or a related field is preferred.

• Familiarity with options, futures, binary contracts, or other exchange-traded products.

The successful candidate will act as the company’s designated Head of Compliance and AMLCO in accordance with applicable CySEC requirements, ensuring that the company maintains effective internal controls, meets its regulatory obligations, and operates in line with the relevant legal and regulatory framework.

This role requires strong knowledge of the Forex/CFD industry, experience dealing with regulatory authorities, and the ability to work closely with the Board of Directors, Senior Management, and operational teams to promote a strong compliance culture.

Responsibilities

• Oversee the company’s compliance framework to ensure adherence to applicable CySEC requirements, EU regulations, and relevant local and international legislation

• Act as a key point of contact with CySEC, MOKAS, and other relevant regulatory authorities, supporting regulatory communications, inspections, and information requests

• Develop, implement, maintain, and periodically review the company’s Anti-Money Laundering and Counter-Terrorist Financing framework in line with applicable requirements

• Conduct and oversee regular AML/CFT business risk assessments, identifying key risks and ensuring appropriate mitigation measures are implemented

• Oversee the effectiveness of customer onboarding controls, including CDD, EDD, beneficial ownership verification, PEP screening, and sanctions screening

• Oversee AML-related transaction monitoring arrangements, ensuring suspicious patterns, unusual transactions, and potential financial crime indicators are identified and appropriately escalated

• Assess escalated cases and ensure suspicious activity reports and other required notifications are submitted to the relevant authorities in accordance with applicable legal obligations

• Develop and execute a risk-based compliance monitoring plan to assess the effectiveness of internal controls, identify deficiencies, and follow up on corrective actions

• Provide compliance guidance on Forex and CFD activities, including client classification, trading-related risks, transaction flows, and potential market abuse or financial crime indicators

• Advise client onboarding, payments, customer support, and transaction monitoring teams on compliance requirements, risk indicators, and escalation procedures

• Monitor changes in applicable laws, regulations, regulatory guidance, and industry practices, assessing their impact on the company and coordinating the implementation of necessary changes

• Organize and deliver regular compliance and AML/CFT training to employees, ensuring staff understand their responsibilities and reporting obligations

• Prepare periodic compliance and AML/CFT reports for senior management and the Board, highlighting key risks, monitoring results, significant cases, regulatory developments, and recommended actions

• Promote a strong compliance culture across the organisation, advise management on regulatory risks, support internal and external audits, and identify opportunities to strengthen the company’s compliance framework

Requirements

• Proven experience in a senior compliance, AML/CFT, or regulatory role within a Forex/CFD brokerage, investment firm, or another regulated financial services institution

• Strong knowledge of CySEC regulatory requirements and the applicable Cyprus and EU AML/CFT framework

• Experience acting as, or working closely with, a designated Compliance Officer and/or AMLCO

• Demonstrated experience managing regulatory relationships, submissions, and communications with CySEC and relevant authorities

• Strong understanding of AML/CFT risk assessments, customer due diligence, enhanced due diligence, suspicious activity reporting, and transaction monitoring

• Experience designing and executing compliance monitoring programmes and overseeing remediation of identified weaknesses

• Familiarity with the risks associated with retail and professional CFD clients, cross-border payments, and international client onboarding

• Excellent analytical, organizational, and problem-solving skills, with strong attention to detail

• Ability to communicate complex regulatory matters clearly to both operational teams and senior stakeholders

• Strong stakeholder management skills and the ability to work independently while maintaining effective collaboration across departments

• Professional integrity, sound judgement, and the ability to handle confidential and sensitive matters appropriately

• AML Certificate and Advanced is considered an advantage

Benefits

• Comprehensive private medical insurance

• Performance-based end-of-year bonus

• Hybrid working arrangement

• Ongoing training and professional development opportunities

• Twenty-one (21) working days of paid annual leave

• Twelve (12) days of paid sick leave

• Opportunity to work in an international work environment

Job Profile: HR Business Partner

Position overview

Job title: HR Business Partner (HRBP)

Department: People

Business unit supported: Revenue

Reports to: CHRO

Direct reports: None

Key stakeholders: Revenue leadership and managers; People Partners team; Administration; Finance; Legal; Talent Acquisition; external EOR, relocation and immigration providers.

Company context
This role combines business partnering for the Revenue unit with hands-on ownership of HR operations: documentation, employment through EOR, and visa and relocation support. It suits someone who can advise leaders strategically and also get the paperwork right.

Key responsibilities

Business partnering

• Act as the main HR point of contact for managers, and translate business goals into people priorities.

• Advise on team structure, workforce planning and headcount in line with the business targets.

• Support performance management, goal setting and feedback cycles, and coach managers on people decisions.

• Partner with Finance and department leadership on the people side of compensation and bonus plans.

• Collect and analyse people data (turnover, engagement, performance) and turn it into recommendations.

Employee relations and communication

• Handle incident management: address negative situations, escalate relevant information, and follow cases through to resolution.

• Mediate conflicts and help build constructive communication between employees and teams.

• Take part in offboarding: run exit interviews and share turnover insights with stakeholders.

• Manage internal transfers and promotions, including moves into management roles.

HR processes and change

• Design, implement and maintain HR processes, adapting them as the company becomes more structured.

• Support change management during reorganisations and process changes.

• Lead HR projects and ad-hoc requests, and run research and consultations when needed.

HR operations and documentation

• Maintain employee documentation and records: contracts, amendments, policies and HRIS data.

• Manage employment of team members hired through Employer of Record (EOR) providers, covering onboarding, contract changes, offboarding and vendor coordination.

• Coordinate visa, work permit and relocation support: prepare documents, work with immigration providers, and track deadlines and renewals.

• Ensure HR practices comply with local labour laws in all countries where we employ people, working with Legal.

• Prepare HR letters and certificates, such as employment confirmations and reference letters.

• Experience supporting sales or other commercial teams is a strong plus.

• Practical experience with EOR providers, visa or work permit processes, and HR documentation.

• Experience in a fast-growing international company.

• English С1; Russian is a plus.

• Confident user of an HRIS (e.g. HiBob) and Google Workspace/MS Office.

Hard skills

• Full HR lifecycle knowledge and the ability to apply it in practice.

• Understanding of commercial team dynamics: sales metrics, incentive plans, quota-driven performance.

• Working knowledge of labour law and employment compliance across several jurisdictions.

• EOR models, immigration and relocation processes.

• Project management and change management.

• Facilitation, moderation and group work.

• Basic HR analytics: collecting, analysing and presenting people data.

• Coaching and mentoring managers.

• Basic understanding of the company's product and tech stack.

Soft skills

• High emotional intelligence and strong communication skills.

• Business acumen and credibility with senior commercial leaders.

• Attention to detail and accuracy with documents and deadlines.

• Resilience and composure in a high-pace environment.

• Ability to handle strategic and operational work at the same time.

• Ownership and independence; drives tasks to completion.

• Adaptability to ongoing internal and external change.

• Strong planning and time management.

• Discretion with confidential information.

About the role
We are seeking an experienced and hands-on Head of Architecture Office to lead our enterprise and solution architecture strategy, ensuring the design and delivery of scalable, secure, and high-performing technology solutions that support business growth and innovation.
This role will oversee architecture governance, technical standards, solution design, and system modernisation initiatives, ensuring consistency, efficiency, and alignment across technology platforms and engineering teams.
As a key technical leader, you will establish architecture best practices, drive technical excellence, and provide strategic direction on complex technology initiatives while fostering collaboration across Engineering, Infrastructure, and Cyber Security teams.
The ideal candidate combines deep technical expertise with strong strategic thinking and leadership capabilities, with the ability to remain hands-on, guide critical architecture decisions, and balance long-term technology vision with practical delivery, operational efficiency, and business priorities.

Responsibility
Enterprise and solution architecture
• Own and maintain the Enterprise Architecture: current state, target state and roadmap, including domain boundaries, integration and API patterns, data flows, resilience and availability targets, and cloud architecture on the AWS multi-account landing zone.
• Lead solution architecture for priority programmes, for example the client platform rebuild, identity and authentication services, copy trading, CRM and back-office modernisation, and platform migrations, producing Architecture Proposals and Architecture Design Documents with clear options, trade-offs and recommendations.
• Run the architecture review process: review and approve Architecture Design Documents from engineering teams, maintain Architecture Decision Records, and ensure decisions are communicated and adopted.
• Confirm technical feasibility of Business Requirement Documents (BRDs) together with Product Engineering and Cyber Security before delivery commitments are made.
Standards, technical acceptance and governance
• Define, publish and maintain architecture standards, development and coding standards, API and integration standards, non-functional requirements and technical acceptance criteria.
• Maintain a single documentation catalogue with owners, entry points and last-updated dates; standards and acceptance evidence must be viewable, not verbal.
• Act as technical acceptance gate for major deliverables and sit on key technology and business governance committees.
• Embed security-by-design and regulatory awareness into architecture: joint design reviews with Cyber Security (threat modelling, authentication and authorisation patterns, data protection, segregation between regulated entities), and support for the Security Exemption process where deviations are proposed.
Refactoring, technical debt and incident architecture
• Own the portfolio of product and system refactoring and migration initiatives: scope, phasing, expected benefits (stability, performance, maintainability, scalability, delivery efficiency), technical risks, legacy constraints and dependencies, with progress and phase outcomes reported against ETA.
• Lead root-cause analysis for major technical and architecture issues and high-risk production incidents, and define both the short-term fix and the long-term architecture solution, with owner, ETA and residual risk.
• Drive cross-team alignment on technical direction so that Product, Engineering, Data and Platform teams build towards the same target architecture.
Delivery, capacity and cost discipline
• Run AO's weekly management cadence with the CTO: pre-read updates covering incidents, priority projects, refactoring progress, standards and documentation, team capacity and cost; every item with owner, ETA, risk and next action.
• Maintain effort and time estimates for programmes and refactoring work, track AO effort by person, role and project, and present internal cost versus market benchmark to support budgeting and resourcing decisions.
• Provide structured, trackable fields on architecture and refactoring work to the Tech PMO dashboard and Data Team, so architecture delivery is measurable alongside the rest of Tech.
People leadership
• Lead and grow the Architecture Office: define roles and responsibilities, and establish review, mentoring and knowledge-sharing rhythms.
• Grow architecture capability across engineering teams through an architecture guild, design-review coaching and reusable patterns and reference implementations.
• Potentially host and lead an AI / emerging-technology architecture function, including responsible-AI and AI-governance considerations with Cyber Security and Compliance.
Stakeholder and vendor management
• Advise the CTO and CEO on technology direction, build-versus-buy decisions and major technical risks.
• Partner with the Heads of Product Engineering, Platform Engineering, Corporate IT, Data and Cyber Security as a peer in the Tech management team.
• Manage architecture engagements with cloud and technology vendors (for example, AWS professional services, ISVs and integration partners).

Requirements
Must-have
• 12+ years in software engineering, including 5+ years in solution or enterprise architecture roles and experience leading architects or an architecture function as a people manager.
• Proven design of distributed, highly available, low-latency systems, ideally trading or financial platforms; deep hands-on AWS expertise (multi-account landing zone, networking and IAM, containers / Kubernetes, event-driven and microservice architectures, resilience and DR).
• Led large-scale refactoring, re-platforming or migration programmes from legacy systems with measurable outcomes in stability, performance or delivery speed.
• Established architecture governance from scratch or matured it significantly: standards, Architecture Decision Records, review boards, technical acceptance criteria and documentation discipline.
• Security-by-design and regulatory awareness: identity and access management (OAuth2 / OIDC, SSO, MFA), data protection, secure SDLC; comfortable being jointly accountable with Cyber Security for the security of designs.
• Cost and estimation discipline: effort and timeline estimation for programmes, cloud cost optimisation, and benchmarking internal cost against market.
• Hands-on credibility: reviews code and designs, prototypes when needed, and can go deep with senior engineers on any tier of the stack.
• Executive-level communication; structured written pre-reads and clear decision framing.
• Professional proficiency in Mandarin (spoken and written) is required, as the role works day to day with engineering and business teams in Greater China.
Highly regarded
• CFD / FX brokerage domain: MT4 / MT5 ecosystem (server, manager API, bridges and liquidity), CRM and back-office, payment service providers, KYC / AML integrations, copy trading and social trading.
• Data and AI architecture: data platforms, streaming, LLM and agentic application patterns, model and AI governance.
• Experience operating under ASIC, CySEC, MAS or comparable regulatory regimes, including operational resilience and outsourcing / cloud requirements.
• Certifications such as AWS Solutions Architect Professional, TOGAF or equivalent.
• Experience leading distributed engineering teams across Australia and Asia.

Benefits
• Competitive salary and performance-based bonuses.
• Opportunities for career growth and development within a global company.
• Collaborative and inclusive work environment with exposure to cross-region operations.
• Health and wellness benefits.
• Flexible working arrangements.

About the Role

Crypto financial markets generate enormous arbitrage opportunities, signals, and price dislocations every day — but most users lack the expertise to act on them. The AI Strategy Engineer we're looking for is someone who can transform these opportunities into executable AI-powered applications: one-click arbitrage, automated yield optimization, AI trading signals — giving ordinary users access to strategy capabilities that were previously reserved for institutional players.

You will lead strategy research, design, and deployment — developing deep expertise in funding rate arbitrage, basis trading, stablecoin yield strategies, cross-exchange arbitrage, and more. You will combine quantitative strategy logic with AI Agent execution frameworks to build automated systems that directly drive user retention and asset growth. This isn't a pure quant role, nor a pure engineering role — you need to understand markets, understand strategies, and know how to turn them into products users can actually use.

Key Responsibilities

•

Quantitative Strategy Research & Design: Research executable arbitrage opportunities in crypto markets including funding rate arbitrage, basis trading (perpetuals vs. delivery), stablecoin yield strategies (stablecoin lending loops, Launchpool hedging), and cross-exchange arbitrage. Complete strategy logic design, historical backtesting, and risk-adjusted return validation.

•

AI Strategy Application Development: Package quantitative strategies into user-facing AI applications. Design execution workflows, trigger conditions, position management, and risk controls for scenarios such as one-click arbitrage, automated yield optimization, and promotional opportunity capturing. Integrate AI Agent capabilities to enable automated strategy analysis, decision-making, and execution.

•

Market Signal & Intelligence System: Build a multi-source market intelligence capability integrating exchange market data, on-chain data, and community sentiment signals. Use AI models to identify hot opportunities, entry timing, and take-profit/stop-loss strategies, providing users with disciplined, AI-assisted trading signals.

•

Strategy Risk Control & Position Management: Design risk frameworks for each strategy class, including maximum drawdown controls, dynamic position calibration, and circuit breakers for extreme market conditions. Regularly analyze live strategy performance, identify degradation factors, and drive iterative optimization.

•

Strategy Productization for User Scenarios: Develop a deep understanding of different user personas (conservative yield-seekers vs. active traders) and translate strategy capabilities into perceivable product value — defining the core interaction logic, return visualization, and risk communication for strategy applications.

•

Cross-System Strategy Integration: Collaborate with engineering teams to integrate strategies with exchange APIs (including third-party exchanges), and drive the engineering delivery of automated strategy execution with unified cross-exchange asset management.

Requirements

•

Quantitative Strategy Experience: 3+ years of quantitative strategy research or trading experience, with at least one strategy class delivered end-to-end in production (funding rate arbitrage, basis trading, statistical arbitrage, market-neutral, etc.); proficient with backtesting frameworks and able to independently conduct strategy validation and attribution analysis.

•

Deep Crypto Market Knowledge: Strong command of crypto derivatives market mechanics including perpetual contract funding rates, delivery futures basis dynamics, stablecoin protocol yield structures (USDE / USD1 / BYUSD etc.), and DeFi protocol return mechanisms. Live trading strategy experience is strongly preferred.

•

Programming & Data Analysis: Proficient in Python for strategy development and data analysis (Pandas / NumPy / backtesting frameworks); experience with exchange API integration; able to work with market tick data, funding rate history, and other quantitative datasets.

•

AI / Agent Integration: Hands-on experience building LLM applications or AI Agents; able to encapsulate strategy logic as agent-callable tools and construct automated strategy pipelines from signal analysis through decision-making to execution.

•

Business Acumen & Product Thinking: Able to identify actionable strategy opportunities from a user-value perspective and translate complex quantitative strategies into understandable, actionable product experiences; capable of independently driving strategy concepts from 0 to 1.

Nice to Have

•

Live trading experience with cross-exchange arbitrage (funding rate, cross-exchange spread, basis arbitrage) or on-chain DeFi strategies.

•

Familiarity with on-chain analytics tools (Dune / Nansen / Glassnode) for mining strategy signals from on-chain indicators.

•

Experience developing and operating automated trading systems (quant trading bots, grid strategies, DCA systems, etc.).

•

Understanding of AI-driven signal generation, with practical experience combining market sentiment and quantitative models.

Exchange Platform Performance

Optimize order entry, risk, matching and market data processing paths.

•

Identify bottlenecks across order validation, risk checks, matching, execution reporting and market data publication.

•

Improve latency, throughput, jitter and scalability.

•

Translate exchange and market-structure requirements into high-performance designs.

•

Evaluate trade-offs between performance, resilience and maintainability.

Low-Latency Architecture and Software

•

Design architectures and data flows for latency-critical exchange components.

•

Optimize concurrency, thread scheduling, memory access and data structures.

•

Apply cache-efficient design, memory alignment, allocation avoidance and zero-copy processing.

•

Design lock-free or wait-free algorithms and high-performance queues.

•

Reduce unnecessary processing, copying, serialization and context switching.

Design and optimize binary protocols and communication between gateways, risk engines, matching engines and market data components.

Improve serialization, IPC, messaging, buffering, batching and backpressure handling.

Evaluate technologies such as Aeron, TIBCO FTL, DPDK and Solarflare OpenOnload.

Optimize NIC queues, interrupts, packet processing and memory buffers.

•

Apply CPU isolation, thread pinning, IRQ affinity and NUMA-aware resource allocation.

•

Analyze cache behavior, context switches, page faults, microbursts, queueing and tail-latency variation.

•

Collaborate with Infrastructure Engineering on Linux, firmware, BIOS, NIC and server configuration.

•

Establish representative benchmarks for exchange workloads.

•

Measure component and end-to-end latency, including p50, p99, p99.9 and p99.99.

•

Build profiling, tracing and automated performance-regression capabilities.

•

Investigate latency spikes, jitter and throughput limitations.

•

Reproduce production performance issues and translate findings into engineering improvements.

•

Use reliable performance evidence to guide architecture and protocol decisions.

Experience building or optimizing production trading systems with latency below 100 microseconds.

Experience with order entry gateways, market data distribution, risk engines or matching engines.

•

Experience profiling latency-critical systems and analyzing latency distributions.

•

Ability to investigate performance across application, protocol, network, operating-system and hardware layers.

•

Strong hands-on technical expertise in:

•

C++ and Java

•

Linux systems

•

Networking

•

Concurrency

•

Low-latency architecture

•

Memory optimization

•

Lock-free systems

•

Binary protocols

•

Tail-latency optimization

•

Experience with FIX, FIXP, SBE or proprietary exchange protocols.

•

Experience with Aeron, TIBCO FTL or similar messaging technologies.

•

Experience with DPDK, Solarflare OpenOnload or equivalent user-space networking.

•

Knowledge of SPSC/MPSC queues, NUMA, huge pages, CPU pinning and cache-line optimization.

Familiarity with Linux perf, eBPF, flame graphs and hardware performance counters.

Understanding of exchange market structure, order lifecycle, pre-trade risk, matching engines and market data distribution.

We are seeking an experienced, hands-on strategic and operational leader to head the Financial Intelligence Unit (FIU) globally across every jurisdiction where Crypto.com operates. This role owns the end-to-end global financial crime transaction monitoring and investigation lifecycle, functioning as an integrated process chain spanning strategy, policy and procedure design, transaction monitoring rules design and management, transaction monitoring technology, Level 1 quality and SLA governance, Level 2 complex investigations, risk mitigation decisions, and SAR/STR filings across sanctions, AML/CFT, fraud, and complex fiat/crypto typologies.
You will set the global strategy, policies, and implementation procedures; continuously adapt the program to evolving financial crime risks; and assess Crypto.com’s overall transactional financial crime risk posture. Combining deep financial crime expertise with rigorous operational and process discipline, you will directly lead the global rules design, transaction monitoring, investigations, and SARs teams across North America, EMEA, and APAC, while exercising functional oversight over Level 1 alert operations by setting their procedures, monitoring their SLAs, and governing their output quality. You will own our transaction monitoring platforms, maintain real-time operational dashboards, and remain directly involved in complex casework, data analysis, and written work product. Additionally, the role includes interfacing with regulators during examinations and supporting law enforcement and financial intelligence unit engagements. Reporting to the SVP, Compliance in the US, you will partner closely with regional compliance teams, Operations, Data, and Product leadership to keep Crypto.com’s defenses ahead of emerging threats.


Key Responsibilities
Global FIU Strategy & Operating Model

• Define and own the multi-year global FIU strategy, target operating model, and investigative standards, aligned to the firm’s licensing footprint, product roadmap, and regulatory risk appetite.

• Manage the full transactional financial crime process chain, from rule design and alert generation through triage, escalation, investigation, risk mitigation, and SAR/STR reporting, ensuring global consistency with appropriate local tailoring.

• Continuously assess Crypto.com’s overall financial crime posture from a transactional risk perspective, proactively adapting rules, workflows, and controls to evolving money laundering, sanctions evasion, fraud, and terrorist financing typologies.

• Own the global FIU budget, headcount plan, vendor strategy (blockchain analytics, case management, data providers), and capacity forecasting across regions.

Investigations, SAR/STR Oversight & Regulatory Interface

Your Role in Our Mission
As an Executive – FNmarkets, you are responsible for running the reconciliation cycle across CRM, core transaction platform, and Payment Service Provider (PSP) platforms for NEXT Bangladesh—enabling a twice-daily reconciliation standard that catches discrepancies on the same day. You also own ApprovalMax bill processing, withdrawable profit calculations, periodic management and regulatory financial reporting, and performance dashboard maintenance. Working alongside the Senior Executive and Internal Audit Executive, you support PSP and Xero processing, revenue and partner entries, and Back Office withdrawal reviews to uphold audit readiness, regulatory compliance, and timely, accurate reporting.

How You’ll Make an Impact (Key Responsibilities)
1. Reconciliation Cycle (CRM, Core Platform & PSP)
•
Daily Execution: Own and execute the daily reconciliation cycle across CRM, core transaction platform, and PSP platforms for NEXT Bangladesh.
•
Discrepancy Resolution: Identify, document, and escalate same-day discrepancies, including CRM vs. core platform balance mismatches and PSP settlement variances.
•
Midday Cut-Off: Complete the cycle by the defined midday cut-off, creating a clean mid-day checkpoint ahead of the closing cycle.
•
Audit Readiness: Maintain audit-ready reconciliation logs in line with regulatory and internal control requirements.
2. PSP Transaction Processing & Xero Upload
•
Daily Categorization: Identify and categorize PSP deposits, withdrawals, and fees daily.
•
Xero Uploads: Upload PSP transactions into Xero on a daily basis.
•
Monthly Reconciliation: Perform monthly PSP reconciliation and balance checks under the Senior Executive’s review.
3. Revenue & Partner Entry Support
•
Daily Entries: Assist in daily revenue recognition, partner profitability, and negative balance uploads to Xero.
•
Accuracy & Timeliness: Support the Senior Executive in maintaining the accuracy and timeliness of daily entries.

•
Payables Management: Process and manage bills for NEXT Bangladesh through the ApprovalMax workflow.
•
Approval Routing: Ensure all payables are submitted, routed, and approved in line with internal approval hierarchies and entity-level controls.
•
Close Documentation: Maintain accurate records of processed bills for audit and month-end close.
•
Withdrawable Profit: Calculate withdrawable profit from client balances in line with internal policies and platform rules, submitting within defined timelines to support Operations and PT operations.
5. Financial Reporting & Performance Dashboard
•
Management & Regulatory Reporting: Prepare and submit periodic management reporting packs and regulatory financial reports for NEXT Bangladesh within defined deadlines.

Dashboard Maintenance: Maintain and update the performance dashboard with key financial metrics, including revenue, partner profitability, reconciliation status, and PSP settlement balances.

Payward - the parent company behind Kraken, NinjaTrader, Breakout,  xStocks, Payward Services and CF Benchmarks - has spent the last 15 years building one of the most modern and globally accessible financial infrastructure platforms in the industry, built to advance an open, global financial system.




THE TEAM

Founded in 2011, Kraken is one of the world's longest-standing crypto platforms, trusted by over 10 million individuals and institutions across the globe. It offers spot trading, margin, futures, staking, and OTC services, with products built for both individual investors and institutional clients.

The opportunity
Consumer Growth helps customers get more value from the Kraken app. We improve how people discover relevant features, build confidence using them, and keep coming back. We work closely with Product, Design and Data to understand customer behavior, identify opportunities and test ideas.

Our engineers help shape what we build. You’ll bring ideas to the table, challenge assumptions and own your work from the initial hypothesis through launch, measurement and iteration.

Ship fast experiments, from a couple of days to a couple of weeks, to improve conversion and retention in the Kraken app.

 - Find funnel drop-offs and turn them into testable ideas, then build, measure and iterate.

 - Design, develop and maintain high-quality React Native features for our consumer mobile app.

 - Help customers discover and adopt relevant features through improvements to customer journeys, incentives and A/B tests.

 - Use AI to build quickly, then review and ship with a high quality bar.

 - Deliver polished, user-friendly UI that makes the product feel great to use.

 - Build for correctness, accessibility, performance and reliability, with testing appropriate to the change.

 - Work closely with Product, Design, Data and Backend Engineering to define hypotheses and measure results.

 - Instrument your work so the team can evaluate customer behavior and experiment results, and use what you learn to improve, expand or stop an experiment.

 - Turn successful experiments into reliable, maintainable product experiences.

 - Proactively spot gaps and opportunities, and take ownership of the outcome.

 
 


WHAT YOU BRING

 - Strong experience building production mobile apps with React Native and TypeScript.

 - A product and growth mindset, focused on moving metrics rather than just shipping code.

 - Evidence of product impact: you can explain what you built, why you built it and what you learned after launch.

 - Curiosity about data, and comfort using analytics tools such as Mixpanel and Segment.

 - Experience working in a scale-up or other high-growth, fast-moving environment.

 - Fluency in using AI tools to build, review and ship code, while retaining ownership of engineering decisions and the quality of the result.

 - A strong eye for UI quality and polish.

 - A self-directed approach, with the confidence to find problems and fix them without being asked.

 - Comfort working from an ambiguous customer problem, proposing ideas and finding a small, useful change to test.

 - Collaborative working style across Product, Design and Engineering.

 - Strong written and verbal communication skills in English.

 


NICE TO HAVES

 - Hands-on experience running A/B tests and experiments, ideally with Statsig or a similar tool.

 - Experience with large-scale consumer products used by millions of people.

 - Agency or consulting background shipping across multiple products.

 - Experience in consumer fintech, payments or crypto apps.

 
 
 
 



Unless a specific application deadline is stated in the job posting, applications are accepted on an ongoing basis.

Please note, applicants are permitted to redact or remove information on their resume that identifies age, date of birth, or dates of attendance at or graduation from an educational institution.

We consider qualified applicants with criminal histories for employment on our team, assessing candidates in a manner consistent with the requirements of the San Francisco Fair Chance Ordinance.




OUR COMMITMENT

Payward is powered by people from around the world and we celebrate the diverse talents, backgrounds, contributions, and unique perspectives that everyone brings to the table. We hire based on merit, seeking out people with the right abilities, knowledge, and skills for the job. We encourage you to apply for roles where you don't fully meet the listed requirements, especially if you're passionate or knowledgeable about crypto.


We may ask candidates to complete job-related skills or work-style assessments as part of our hiring process. These assessments evaluate competencies relevant to the role and are applied consistently across candidates for similar positions. Results are considered alongside experience and interviews, and are not the sole basis for any employment decision.


As an equal opportunity employer, we don't tolerate discrimination or harassment of any kind, whether based on race, ethnicity, age, gender identity, citizenship, religion, sexual orientation, disability, pregnancy, veteran status, or any other protected characteristic as outlined by federal, state, or local laws.

How do we work?

Hello Everyone!

You’ll join an in-house Creative Team based in our Warsaw (Poland) or Prague (Czechia) office, reporting into the Head of Creative Production. You will play a crucial role in publishing and managing high-volume content across our websites and digital platforms, and in supporting the technical setup and migration of our content management systems.

The role requires a solid understanding of the brand, the product and the market we compete in. Knowledge of trading is advantageous but not essential, as training will be given.

We work in a hybrid model - we'd love to meet you in the office 2 times a week with respect to your own commitments.

In this role, you will:

• Drive the use of AI in how we create, manage and publish content. You will identify, test and roll out AI-assisted workflows, with human review.

• Manage page templates, metadata, taxonomy, navigation and media libraries, and keep content accurate, accessible and SEO-friendly.
• Support the migration to our new CMS, including content audits, content modelling and mapping, clean-up, and redirect planning. You will look for ways to optimize the work, question existing processes with smart thinking, and deliver automated solutions that fit the scope of the project.
• Help manage the CMS and its environments, including user roles and permissions, integrations, and staging and production workflows.
• Run QA and UAT before and after go-live (broken links, rendering, forms, analytics tags and performance).
• Work closely with copywriters, designers, developers and marketing to take projects from brief to final delivery.
• Document processes and train colleagues on CMS best practice.

What skillsets do you need to be successful in this role?

• 3+ years of experience in a similar position, in a client-side (in-house) or agency environment, but impact matters more than years.
• Hands-on experience publishing and managing content in a CMS (e.g. Wagtail, WordPress, Drupal, AEM, Sitecore, Contentful or similar).
• Experience supporting or delivering a CMS migration or replatforming project.
• Experience using AI tools to improve content workflows and migration tasks, with strong human oversight and a clear eye on accuracy and compliance.
• Working knowledge of HTML and CSS. Basic scripting or SQL for bulk content tasks is a plus.
• Understanding of technical SEO, including URL structure, redirects, metadata and site performance.
• Fluent English, with excellent written and verbal communication skills.
• Keeps up to date with CMS, content and web publishing trends and best practice.
• Ability to work in a fast-paced environment, manage multiple projects, and adapt to changing priorities.
• Autonomy and excellent organisation and project management skills.
• Candidates are asked to share examples of their previous work, such as live pages they have published, migration or CMS projects, or a case study.

Nice to have:

• Familiarity with web analytics and tag management tools (e.g. GA4, Google Tag Manager) and a working understanding of APIs and version control.
• Experience of Jira or similar project management tools.
• Interest in or experience of working in financial services (banking, FX, CFDs), gambling or other regulated industries.

Enterprise Efficiency builds the internal products and platforms that power how our company operates across People, Finance, Governance, Risk and Compliance (GRC), Legal, Procurement, and related functions.

Turn domain expertise into enterprise products. Understand your function’s processes, policies, controls, and user needs. Translate them into internal products that simplify daily work and support business operations at scale.

Drive efficiency through automation and AI. Identify, test, and scale capabilities that reduce repetitive work and improve decision quality, enabling your function to handle growing demand without proportional increases in manual effort.

7+ years of experience in product management or closely related enterprise product roles, including experience leading product managers and managing a portfolio across teams.

A track record of taking enterprise products from discovery through launch, adoption, and measurable business outcomes.

Deep functional expertise in at least one of the following domains, with experience leading initiatives across adjacent functions:

Finance: FP&A, procurement-to-pay, record-to-report, accounting operations, or financial controls.

People: Core HR, recruiting, employee lifecycle, performance, compensation processes, or workforce planning.

•

GRC: Risk assessment, control management, audit, policy management, third-party risk, or remediation.

Demonstrated ability to translate complex business processes, policies, and controls into clear product models, workflows, and system requirements.

Experience defining product strategy, allocating resources, and making difficult prioritization and build-versus-buy decisions.

Technical fluency in enterprise integrations, data dependencies, identity, permissions, and auditability.

•

Strong executive communication and stakeholder leadership, including the ability to challenge assumptions and align teams without direct authority.

Experience building or transforming an enterprise product organization.

Experience with platforms such as Workday, Oracle, SAP, ServiceNow, or equivalent internal systems.

Experience deploying AI or agent capabilities into production workflows and measuring their business impact.

Experience in financial services, crypto, payments, or another environment with demanding control and audit requirements.

Experience building reusable platforms and consolidating fragmented internal tools.

The Account team owns how every OKX user first gets in and keeps getting in safely. We build the identity and access foundation that every other product depends on. That foundation has to scale to millions of users across regions and be resilient against constant attack, while still feeling easy to use. Every control we build has to be consistent in how it's enforced, complete in what it covers, and explainable when it acts.

What You'll Be Doing

•

Formulate, select and develop technical designs across the account domain. That includes registration and onboarding, login and multi-factor authentication, passwordless login, third-party and single sign-on, session and device management, account recovery, sub-account and institutional account structures, and account lifecycle controls such as freezing, closure and data retention.

•

Build AI/ML-powered features such as account-takeover detection, suspicious-login detection, automated attack and bot defense, risk-based authentication, smarter recovery flows, and support-assist tools for account issues.

技术前瞻与团队赋能：持续追踪 Agent 领域前沿进展，将研究成果转化为 AI 工程实践；制定团队 Agent 开发规范与最佳实践，通过 Code Review、技术分享与方向评审推动团队整体 AI-native 工程能力提升。

Crypto.com is a global cryptocurrency platform serving traders and investors in markets around the world. The CDC product line is our international crypto trading app — spanning spot, perpetual contracts, and card rips — and we are building the next generation of trading products for a global audience.

We’re looking for a Senior Manager, Growth to sit at the intersection of user acquisition, creative strategy, martech, and measurement. This is not a single-lane role. You’ll own the day-to-day performance of our UA program across paid channels and every market we operate in, but you’ll also lead three critical sub-functions — creative, martech, and measurement — that today sit with senior leadership and need a dedicated operator to take them to the next level.

You’ll work directly with our agency partners, product teams, data science, and platform reps (Meta, Google, Apple) across regions. You’ll inherit a scaled UA program with multiple products launching simultaneously, a global market footprint, and a martech stack that’s being built in real time. If you’re the kind of person who can context-switch between a Meta CAPI payload spec and a creative brief in the same afternoon, this role was made for you.

Responsibilities 
User Acquisition Operations

• Own the weekly operating rhythm for CDC paid UA — spend plans, pacing, optimization decisions, and performance reporting across all channels (Meta, Google, Apple Search, programmatic DSPs, affiliates, regional platforms, and emerging networks), across every market we operate in

• Manage the relationship with our performance agency on a daily basis — standups, creative briefings, channel strategy, spend allocation, and trading decisions

• Drive channel-level optimization using CAC, CPFT, pLTV ROAS, and lower-funnel conversion metrics. You’re expected to know what’s working, what’s not, and why before anyone asks

• Lead GTM execution for new product launches and market openings (spot, perpetual contracts, card rips, new offer structures) — from tracking readiness through creative production through spend activation

• Build and maintain the weekly trading deck and leadership updates. Present performance narratives to VP and C-level stakeholders with clarity and confidence

• Own the competitive monitoring cadence — Sensor Tower, app store rankings, ad intelligence — across key markets, and translate competitive signals into channel and creative decisions

• Own market prioritisation — which countries we open, in what order, and what each market needs in localisation, payment rails, and channel mix before we commit spend

Sub-function: Creative Strategy

Our creative pipeline is currently managed between agency and leadership. This role takes ownership of the full creative lifecycle for performance marketing.

• Own the creative learning agenda — what hooks, formats, and concepts we’re testing, what’s winning, and what to kill. Maintain a structured view of creative performance by channel, format, and audience

• Lead creative briefing for the agency and UGC creators. Translate product updates, offers, and cultural moments into production-ready briefs with clear deliverables and timelines, localised for each market we run in

• Drive format expansion beyond static display — UGC video, social-native content, meme-format creative, and AI-assisted production pipelines

• Establish a rapid refresh cadence to combat creative fatigue across channels, and ensure channel-specific sizing and placement specs are met

• Coordinate with brand and content teams on production shoots, scripting, and asset capture for UA use

Sub-function: Martech

Our martech stack spans AppsFlyer, Segment, Firebase, Google Tag Manager, Meta CAPI, Impact (affiliates), and multiple ad platform integrations. Today this is led by our VP with execution support from a solo martech lead. This role becomes the strategic owner.

• Serve as the growth team’s primary point of contact for all tracking, attribution, and signal infrastructure. You’re the person who knows whether events are firing, payloads are complete, and platform signals are flowing

• Partner with our martech lead to prioritize and unblock implementation work — new product event instrumentation, platform pixel/CAPI builds, conversion upload pipelines, and deep link configuration

• Own the relationship with platform measurement teams (Google gTech, Meta measurement partners, AppsFlyer TAMs) across regions and ensure their recommendations translate into shipped work

• Drive martech readiness for every product launch and offer change. If tracking isn’t ready, you’re the one who flags it and owns the escalation

• Understand the full signal chain from user action to ad platform optimization loop — SDK events, server-to-server integrations, CAPI payloads, consent parameters, and AEM eligibility requirements

• Handle the multi-market layer — regional MMP configuration, multi-currency revenue handling, and market-specific consent and privacy regimes

Sub-function: Measurement

Measurement maturity is the constraint on scaling. This role owns the roadmap for closing attribution gaps and building toward incrementality-based decision-making.

• Own the attribution framework — last-click, MECE logic, promo code overlap rules — and ensure it’s consistently applied across reporting, agency data, and leadership updates

• Define and maintain measurement plans for each product line (spot, perps, rips) including KPI definitions, LTV attribution windows, and what “success” looks like at each funnel stage

• Lead the build-out of conversion feedback loops for each platform — Google Ads click ID upload pipelines, Meta CAPI integration, and Apple SKAN/AdAttributionKit readiness

• Partner with data science on pLTV model validation, cohort economics tracking, and the eventual transition from CPA to ROAS-based bidding

• Scope and prioritize incrementality testing (geo holdouts, per-channel lift measurement) and marketing mix modeling as the program matures

• Maintain reporting credibility — when agency data and Tableau data don’t match, you’re the person who investigates, explains, and fixes it

• Normalise reporting across currencies and markets so performance is comparable country to country, and so a CAC in one region means the same thing as a CAC in another

Requirements: 
• 5+ years in performance marketing or growth, with direct ownership of paid UA budgets across Meta, Google, Apple Search, and at least one programmatic partner

• Hands-on experience with mobile measurement partners (AppsFlyer, Adjust, or Branch), server-to-server integrations, and ad platform conversion APIs (Meta CAPI, Google Ads S2S)

• Experience marketing trading or investing products — you understand funding rates, spreads, deposit and withdrawal flows, and why an active trader’s value profile looks different from a casual user’s

• Track record running paid UA across multiple international markets — localisation, regional channel mix, a multi-time-zone operating rhythm, and market-by-market regulatory nuance

• Strong working knowledge of attribution models, SKAN/AdAttributionKit, AEM eligibility, and the privacy-era signal landscape

• Experience managing or closely partnering with a performance creative function — you’ve briefed UGC creators, reviewed ad concepts, and made data-backed creative decisions

• Comfort with ambiguity and competing priorities. You’ll be launching multiple products, fixing attribution gaps, and building new measurement infrastructure simultaneously

• Exceptional communication skills — you can explain a CAPI payload issue to an engineer and a CAC trend to a CMO in the same day

• Experience in crypto, trading, fintech, or financial services is strongly preferred — you’ve marketed a product where the user is putting capital at risk. What matters most is that you’ve scaled paid UA in a high-velocity, multi-product environment

Why This Role: 
• You’re joining at an inflection point — new products launching, measurement stack being built, creative pipeline evolving. The person in this seat will shape how all of it comes together

• You’ll have real ownership across UA, creative, martech, and measurement. This is not a channel manager role — it’s a multi-discipline growth operator role with a clear path to director

• You’ll work with a small, senior team that moves fast and makes real decisions. No layers of approval — the VP is your skip and the CMO is one level above that

• Part of Crypto.com — a global platform with the resources and ambition to build a category-defining product, and the speed and autonomy of a startup growth team

• Global remit — the markets you open and the playbooks you build will define how we scale internationally, not just in one country
